newsitem.title: USA: Toyota seeks to block Republic dealership buys.
newsitem.headline: Toyota seeks to block Republic dealership buys.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. said Monday it filed another lawsuit to prevent Florida billionaire H. Wayne Huizenga's Republic Industries Inc. from acquiring more of its dealerships.

The Japanese automaker's Toyota Motor Sales USA Inc. subsidiary filed a complaint in Florida seeking to block Republic from buying Lexus of Tampa Bay and an affiliated Lexus dealership of Clearwater, Fla., both owned by Gulf Management Inc.

In the complaint filed with the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, Toyota alleged Republic has failed to comply with the company's established franchise requirements and policies.
Toyota alleged that because Republic failed to comply, and for other reasons, the company is not qualified to own the Gulf Management Lexus dealerships under Florida law.

"The rapid acquisition of a large number of dealerships by a single enterprise could seriously harm our other dealers and customers, as well as our business," said Yale Gieszl, Toyota Motor Sales executive vice president.
"Since January 1997, Republic's been on an unprecedented dealership buying spree, moving from no ownership to reportedly more than 120 separate new car franchises," said Gieszl.

Toyota is suing Republic in Arizona, Florida and Texas in an effort to slow Republic's rapid accumulation of auto dealerships. Toyota policy limits any single entity to ownership of seven Toyota stores and three Lexus stores, as a way to maintain quality control.
Republic, which in a short period has become the nation's largest auto dealer, was not immediately available for comment.
Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based Republic's stock edged down 6 cents to $23.06 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
